sections.content:
This course content is structured into three core phases: Analysis, Formulation, and Implementation — each covering strategic management modules tailored to different stages of business strategy:
Analysis (Phase 1) includes 3 modules focused on evaluating foundational contexts: Module 1 (PESTEL for environmental analysis), Module 2 (Porter’s Five Forces + Industry Life Cycle for industry analysis), and Module 3 (Vision/Mission/Values + VRIO for internal firm analysis).
Formulation (Phase 2) builds on analysis with 4 modules centered on strategy design: Modules 4 (cost leadership/differentiation business strategies) and 5 (business models) at the business level, plus Modules 6 (vertical integration/diversification) and 7 (mergers/acquisitions) at the corporate level.
Implementation (Phase 3) wraps up with Module 8, which covers corporate governance (the framework for executing strategy).

sections.content:
MGMT 4210 introduces concepts and analytical techniques for creating a sustainable advantage in difficult
competitive environments. The perspective adopted for this course is that of the top manager who has
overall responsibility for the performance of the firm or of a business unit within the firm. Such a manager
needs to understand the basis for the current performance of the firm and to identify those changes (inside
or outside the firm) that are most likely to affect future performance adversely or that provide opportunities
for the firm to improve its performance. The manager must then use the firm’s resources to formulate and
implement strategies to compete successfully in its new environment. The strategy must define the scope
of the firm’s activities, the logic through which the activities result in better performance, and what it is
about the firm that allows it to carry out those activities better than its competitors. Having a solid
understanding of strategy is not only vital for top managers, but is also important for external consultants,
auditors, financial analysts, and bankers in evaluating and valuing other firms.

sections.teaching:
Jaeho teaches really well. His articulation and intonation is good, and his presentation is engaging. It is unlike other modules where you sit in the lecture theatre listening to the professor for the whole duration. He presents a case study of a company every week, and gives us the time to break out into our groups to discuss about the case study, then he will link the case studies to the concepts that he is teaching. Overall, he is a great lecturer.

This is arguably my best lecture in my whole university life. I hope to attend his classes again, if I had the chance. As he mentioned at the start of the course, "The course would be FUN and INTENSE". True and behold, he really made the course FUN and INTENSE.
sections.grading: I feel the bell curve for this module is pretty high as many people can score high marks in the individual case analyses. The differentiating factor could be your class participation. If he remembers you, it would definitely be a good thing for you.
sections.workload:
The workload is pretty high for a 3-credit course. The workload is tough due to the pre-readings prior to the lectures. They could easily be over 20 pages.

In addition, from lecture 5/6 onwards, there are weekly case presentations, and you have to choose 3 out of 8 to submit. The cases are not easy, as they can go as high as 28 pages.

If you are taking this course, be prepared to work super damn hard if you wanna be on the right side of the bell curve. Nonetheless, you will have a great time attending this course despite the workload.

Class content is focused around strategy and different frameworks that can be used and applied to help a firm achieve superior, sustainable performance, and create value for all share/stakeholders involved. Interesting content that's taught in a way that is deeply linked to real life situations and cases, so makes it easy to digest and understand.

Content covers both the internal and external environment of the firm, and allows for students to get a deep understanding of how these influence and contribute to a firm's competitive advantage.
sections.teaching:
JT is a really knowledgable, kind, and funny professor. He breaks down very complex and technical terms and situations into simpler, easier to digest, and understandable terms. During class, he provides ample examples and opportunities for us to apply concepts and frameworks to real life situations, which is helpful for understanding how they work and why they would be useful.

I really got the feeling that he wanted us to learn and was personally very invested in teaching, and helping us to understand the content and do well. He also would periodically update us on current events that were relevant to the content we covered in class, which allowed us to further develop our knowledge and understanding of 1) the business world and 2) the content in a real life situation.

Overall, he's a really great professor!

sections.content:
Content is actually quite vague. You will need to think like a strategist and evaluate the company by different frameworks and concepts. If the company's policies are not sustainable and profitable, what changes we need to do? There will be 7 cases discussion in total to apply what we have learned from the lectures. The case is quite interesting and useful, but not the lecture.

Chapters included:
1. Introduction & Vision, Mission, and Values
2. Strategic Management Process
3. External Analysis (PESTEL, 5 Forces, SCP etc)
4. Internal Analysis (VRIO, core competencies)
5. Competitive Advantage
6. Business Strategies (Differentiation, cost leadership etc)
7. Corporate Strategy (M&A, Alliances, etc)
8. Global Strategy
9. Organizational Design & Structure
10. Culture, Control & Corporate governance
sections.teaching:
Lectures: Quite boring and quiet
Case: Interesting and intense

Need some time to digest the content.

sections.content: The content for the course is very interesting and useful. It gives a grander understanding of the news that we read. It helps us understand the factors behind key decisions made by companies.
sections.teaching: Professor Pavel encourages students to participate in case discussions. He gives good examples through the lesson and helps understand all concepts easily.
sections.grading: I would say that it is very easy to score well. As long as you do well in the project presentation and report. It might be a bit challenging to come up with the ideas for the project report though. Trying to provide multiple strategies is a safe way to go. But make sure to try to include some details in the suggestions to make them more authentic. Also include materials and concepts from class. The exams were pretty easy.

And the project is done at the end of the semester. hence, the workload is for sure not heavy when compared to a lot of other courses in UST.

sections.content:
A lot of frameworks being introduced in this course and they can be useful during your interview group discussion. Some words being used in the ppt are very difficult to me and made it hard to understand so I have to look up from the dictionary a lot.
A case study pack will be given to students and there will be case discussion in class throughout the semester. the cases are around 10-20 pages long. You will have to read the cases beforehand in order to answer the PRS questions and participate in class.
sections.teaching:
The professor gave a lot of examples in class as he has worked in McKinsey before and knows a lot of things. But then other times he was basically reading powerpoint slides and his accent sometimes makes it hard to listen to what he is talking about.
Also during case discussion, he would jot down the points on papers and uses a projector to show us. But with his messy handwriting, it was difficult to read.
sections.grading:
Attendance: 5
-  IPRS is used at the start of every lesson and it starts sharply when class begins. There will be 3 question related to last class/case study of the day. Usually within the first 5 mins of class so better not to be late. It was said that you will have to answer at least 1q to get full attendance mark.

Participation: 10
- You will have to answer a lot of questions in class and the best chance is during case discussion. And it actually counts a lot. Can affect your subgrade.  

Mid-term exam: 20
- MC with a few short questions.

Final exam: 25
- MC, 5-page case questions and a few long questions. MC was said to be non-cumulative but turns out to be including the Midterm stuff.

Group final project: 40
- including presentation and final report. For the topic, you will have to analyze the corporate strategies of the company that you have chosen and then suggest possible ways to tackle the issues. Groups are being assigned by the prof but he really values peer evaluation, so if you have a serious issue, feel free to show him the proof.

I didn't miss any PRS attendance but should have zero for participation. My midterm was below mean for 2.5 marks, final being 9 marks above mean. Our group project was really good and among the highest. At last, I got an A.
sections.workload:
The workload is not that high in the beginning but as project deadline approaches, you will become very busy especially when you have a lot of free riders in your group. But overall there are only 3 things you need to hand in:
1) interim report - for topic approval and not for grading
2) powerpoint slide
3) A 15-page report
Therefore if you start working on it earlier, the workload should be fine.

sections.content: This course gives you insight on how to externally and internally analyse companies and how they are internally structured. For external, It looks at PESTEL, Porters 5 Forces, SCP Analysis, Industry Dynamics and Competitiveness. For Internal, it looks at Core Competencies, RBV and the VRIO Framework. It moves on to mention the different Business Strategies within business units and Corporate Strategies across boundaries. Then finally it wraps up with Formal Structure, Informal Culture and Governance.
sections.teaching: I loved this professor. He may be a little difficult to understand at times due to his accent, but he is a very knowledgable guy and is very enthusiastic about his course. I think this is one of the reasons I liked this course a lot. He would skip in class, always have a big smile on his face and teach with a lot of passion. He is a very friendly and understanding guy who is always willing to help.
sections.grading:
5% Attendance - In the form of PRS Quizzes - Correct answers do not matter only participating in the PRS quiz matters.
5% Individual Participation
5% Group Participation (Based on Case Studies)
20% Midterm (MCQ)
25% Final (MCQ + Short Answer + Long Answer)
40% Group Project (10 Page Report + 10-15 Minute Presentation).
Professor is quite generous with the grading. Not too sure about the grade distributions though.
sections.workload: Not very heavy workload. The group project definitely involves a lot of research. But you get 15% of your grade for pretty much attending class on time. This course is quite easy and almost everybody does well because of it. The margin for error is extremely low and you need to be on top of everything in order to get a top score in this course. This course is pretty much common sense with additional vocabulary thrown at you. It should not be too tough and I recommend it to all
